site.name: Heme SAP Companion
site.title: Heme SAP Companion — a video lecture for every section of ASH-SAP 9e
site.description: Every one of the 449 sections of the ASH-SAP 9th edition mapped to the lecture that explains it. Built for hematology fellows: society and journal sources, no med-student review videos. Search a section you did not follow, get the video.
site.ogDescription: 449 ASH-SAP sections, each with the page number and the lecture that explains it. Fellowship level only — ASH, EHA, ESH, EBMT, VJHemOnc, journal and academic sources.
site.audience: Hematology fellows and hematologists preparing for board certification

hero.heading: Every section of the book, mapped to the lecture that explains it

stance.title: What this is, and what it is not
stance.intro: This site is an index, not a course of its own. It takes the table of contents of the ASH-SAP 9th edition — 49 chapters, 449 sections — and attaches, to each section, the best lecture on the open web that teaches that specific thing. Three things follow from that, and you should know all three before you rely on it.
stance.outroTitle: How to use it without being misled
stance.outro: Read the book. When a section does not land, come here, find that section by its page number, and watch. Then go back to the book. The videos are not a substitute for ASH-SAP and they are not a source of truth — they are third-party recordings of varying age, and hematology practice moves faster than YouTube does. Anything that drives a treatment decision should be checked against the current ASH, NCCN or ESMO guideline, not against a lecture. Where a section had no video worth linking, the slot is left visibly empty with a note saying what was searched. That is deliberate: an empty slot is information, a padded one is not.

verdicts.concept-1: Curation narrows the quality spread on YouTube. It does not close it, and nothing here was reviewed for teaching.
verdicts.concept-2: On treatment questions this site decays. Check the current guideline, not the video.
verdicts.concept-3: Where the open web has nothing, the slot stays empty and says so.

steps.title: Find the section
steps.body: Search by section title, disease, drug or trial name. Every entry carries its ASH-SAP page number, so you can go straight back to the book.

steps.title: Watch the lecture
steps.body: One core lecture per section, plus supplementary videos tagged mechanism, clinical decision, or trial and guideline. Watch mode embeds through youtube-nocookie.com and keeps a playlist beside the player.

steps.title: Check the evidence
steps.body: Where a recommendation rests on specific trials, the PMIDs are listed and every one of them was fetched from the PubMed API, not recalled from memory.

landing.stanceLede: An index of other people's videos has failure modes a textbook does not. Here are the three that matter.

footer.disclaimer: Not medical advice. This is a study aid for hematology trainees and does not establish standard of care. Videos are third-party recordings whose accuracy and currency this site does not control and cannot warrant; hematology practice changes faster than published lectures do. Verify anything that affects patient care against the current ASH, NCCN or ESMO guideline and the primary literature. Section titles and page numbers refer to the ASH-SAP 9th edition, published by the American Society of Hematology; this site is not affiliated with or endorsed by ASH, reproduces none of the book's text, and is not a substitute for it.
footer.credits: Videos remain the copyright of their YouTube channels; this site stores links and public metadata only, and neither rehosts nor mirrors any of them.

llms.summary: A free index that maps all {units} sections of the ASH-SAP 9th edition (American Society of Hematology Self-Assessment Program, 9e, 2025) to freely available video lectures that teach each section. Aimed at hematology fellows, not medical students. Every video is a third-party YouTube work; this site provides curation and links only, and reproduces none of the book's text.
llms.stanceConclusion: Use it to unstick yourself on a section you did not follow, then return to the book. Do not use it as a source of truth for treatment decisions — check the current guideline instead.
